caption:
A new chapter begins at Bangabhaban. President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has officially started his duties.

President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has officially begun his duties at Bangabhaban, the official residence of the President of Bangladesh.

Upon his arrival at the presidential palace, the President was received with a formal Guard of Honor.

This marks the beginning of his official activities and administrative functions as the head of state.

The event was attended by high-ranking officials and military personnel to mark the official commencement of his tenure.

headline_marked: Historic rise: [[Bangladesh climb to record sixth]] in ICC Test rankings
headline: Historic rise: Bangladesh climb to record sixth in ICC Test rankings
summary: The Tigers reach their highest-ever position in Test cricket, moving ahead of Sri Lanka and Pakistan despite a series-ending defeat to Australia.
details: Bangladesh has climbed three places to reach a record sixth position in the ICC Test rankings. The team now holds 78 rating points, placing them behind Australia, South Africa, New Zealand, India, and England.
This achievement marks a significant milestone, as their previous best ranking was seventh, achieved in May this year following a 2-0 home series victory over Pakistan.
The rise is largely attributed to a historic nine-wicket victory in Darwin during their recent tour of Australia, which boosted their standing despite a series-ending loss in Mackay.
Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto described the climb to number six as a 'massive achievement,' although he noted the team would have felt better had they performed better in the final Test match.
With this jump, Bangladesh has moved ahead of several established teams, including Sri Lanka, Pakistan, the West Indies, and Zimbabwe.
In the World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 table, Bangladesh remains in fourth place with 40 points and a percentage of 55.56, narrowly staying ahead of India.
The Tigers have played six WTC matches in the current cycle, winning three, losing two, and drawing one.
The team's next major challenge will be a two-Test series in South Africa, where they aim to strengthen their position among the world's leading contenders.
caption:
From 7th to 6th! Bangladesh reaches its highest-ever rank in Test cricket history.

Bangladesh has climbed three places to reach a record sixth position in the ICC Test rankings. The team now holds 78 rating points, placing them behind Australia, South Africa, New Zealand, India, and England.

This achievement marks a significant milestone, as their previous best ranking was seventh, achieved in May this year following a 2-0 home series victory over Pakistan.

The rise is largely attributed to a historic nine-wicket victory in Darwin during their recent tour of Australia, which boosted their standing despite a series-ending loss in Mackay.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto described the climb to number six as a 'massive achievement,' although he noted the team would have felt better had they performed better in the final Test match.

With this jump, Bangladesh has moved ahead of several established teams, including Sri Lanka, Pakistan, the West Indies, and Zimbabwe.

In the World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 table, Bangladesh remains in fourth place with 40 points and a percentage of 55.56, narrowly staying ahead of India.

The Tigers have played six WTC matches in the current cycle, winning three, losing two, and drawing one.

The team's next major challenge will be a two-Test series in South Africa, where they aim to strengthen their position among the world's leading contenders.
